request.spec:
Show the activity of the sheet: for every user and every event in the sheet's audit file, one
line <user> <EVENT> <count>, sorted by user then event.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Show the activity of the sheet: for every user and every event in the sheet's audit file, one
line <user> <EVENT> <count>, sorted by user then event.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The sheet's activity is now on the main screen. Pressing "Show activity" lists one line per user and event, `<user> <EVENT> <count>`, sorted by user and then by event (for example `uma RATE_SET 2`). `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec.

**Changes:**
- **Server:** a new `Audit.activity(sheetId)` in `Audit.java` reads the sheet's records from the audit file and counts them by user and event. A new `GET /api/sheets/{sheetId}/activity` endpoint in `AuditController.java` serves the result.
- **Front end:** a new `Activity` component in `features/activity/activity.ts`, built like the existing audit viewer. It has the `activity-show` button and the `activity-line` rows the test uses, plus an `activity-error` message if the read fails. It's added to the home screen right after the audit viewer.

The counts are worked out from the audit file each time you press the button, so nothing new is stored and this feature writes no audit records of its own.
